subject: Acme - Post-call TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Subject: Acme - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Hi John / Jane,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciated the candid discussion about traffic patterns and cost sensitivity. Below is a quick recap of the pain, goals, and the TCO levers we discussed, plus suggested next steps. Please confirm or correct anything I missed.

Summary of pain points
- High per-interaction cost driven by long prompts and high token volume across autocomplete and chat flows.
- Unpredictable bursts that spike costs during peak support hours.
- Budget cap of ~$10k/month for the POC phase.

Goals we heard
- Proof a production integration that stays within ~10k/month for the pilot (estimated traffic profile below).
- Maintain sub-600ms median generation latency for interactive features.
- Validate model quality vs current vendor for retrieval-augmented responses.

Key token/TCO numbers (rough order of magnitude)
- Your stated baseline: ~12M tokens/month (combined prompts + completions) based on current usage.
- Example vendor baseline cost (current): ~$1,800–2,400/month per 1M tokens depending on model tier — rough monthly spend ~21k–28.8k.
- Redwood projected baseline (comparable model): ~12M tokens * $0.0006/token = ~$7,200/month.
- Expected reduction with batching + prefix/KV caching + quantized model variant: 30–55% lower effective token spend. That puts an initial optimized estimate in the ~$3,200–5,000/month band for the same workload, depending on cache hit rate and batch sizes.

TCO levers we recommend for the pilot
- Prefix/KV caching: Cache frequent system prompts and repeated conversation prefixes to cut completion token generation. Target cache hit rates of 25–40% in week 1.
- Dynamic batching: Use 50–100ms aggregation windows for non-interactive flows to increase GPU efficiency without affecting perceived latency for users.
- Model variant routing: Route lower-priority long-running jobs to a quantized 4-bit variant; keep the higher-quality fp16 variant for critical interactive requests.
- Smart routing by SLA: Route burst traffic to lower-cost capacity during off-peak or to dedicated capacity if steady throughput needs it.

Pilot proposal & KPIs
- Duration: 30 days test starting week of July 6.
- Success metrics: average cost <= $10k/month pro-rated, median latency < 600ms, cache hit >= 25%, and qualitative pass on 200 eval prompts.
- Deliverables: weekly TCO report, per-route token breakdown, and automated regression alerts for quality.

Attachments: acme_tco_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — includes a 3-scenario cost model (baseline, optimized, aggressive caching).

Next steps
1) You confirm pilot dates and budget boundaries (reply “OK to start July 6” or propose alternate).
2) Share any procurement timeline / PO contacts so Rafael can coordinate.
3) We’ll spin up a sandbox account, import a small sample of your traffic for calibration, and deliver the week-1 cost baseline report.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short sync if that’s easier.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0142

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligns with our internal view. A few clarifications / asks: 

- Our 12M token estimate is on the high side during initial rollout; realistic pilot traffic will likely be ~6–8M tokens/month, but we want headroom for spikes.
- The $10k/month cap for the pilot is firm from finance. If we can hit the mid-point of your optimized estimate (~$4–5k/mo) that would be ideal.
- Can you confirm the expected engineering lift on our side for caching integration? Our team prefers minimal changes to the prompt flow.
- Security: procurement will want SOC2 evidence and a short dataflow diagram. Can Rafael share the compliance pack?

I’m looping in Jane (ops) who will own procurement. Jane — can you share the procurement timeline and PO contact?

Thanks,
